title: Channels SDK: How to bring your Agent to any Channel (Slack, Microsoft Teams)

content_html:
Getting any agent into messaging platforms like Slack is complex. You create a Slack app, handle its events, format messages to the platform's format, handle deliveries with retries, and so on.

Taking that to production is much harder. Then, if you want to bring it into another messaging platform, you do most of the work again, and again for the next platform.

To remove that manual work, we're excited to release the Channels SDK, which brings any AG-UI agent to any channel from one codebase, with a persistence layer so it keeps its memory and context.

Today, we will bring an agent into Slack, learn how everything works along with the architecture, the core patterns and connecting it to real tools like Notion using MCP.

npx copilotkit@latest channels setup

To try the agent live, we have created public channels on Slack and MS Teams. Head to copilotkit.ai/try-channels and we'll get you in.

What you will build

A Slack bot running on your own agent, that can:

  • answer in a thread with the context already around it
  • act through real tools (Notion over MCP)
  • reply with native cards
  • ask for approval before it changes anything
  • read files and images people drop in
  • remember a user across conversations and platforms

Prefer a complete working example? Clone OpenTag on GitHub.

If you want to explore on your own, read the Channels docs, or copy a ready-made prompt from the docs homepage and your coding agent builds your first channel with you.

What is the Channels SDK?

The Channels SDK is an open source TypeScript library that takes any AG-UI agent into Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp and other channels, from one codebase.

npm i @copilotkit/channels

It's built on the AG-UI protocol, so the app and the agent stay decoupled.

You can bring any AG-UI compatible agent framework (LangChain, Google ADK, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Claude Agent SDK, etc.) and swap it later without touching the channel code.

And if you don't want to bring your own framework, we ship a BuiltInAgent that runs on any model, hosted or local (via Ollama, LM Studio, or vLLM). We will be using this for the setup.

You write replies as <Message> JSX, and each platform renders them natively: Block Kit in Slack, Adaptive Cards in Teams.

Managed Path for Slack and Microsoft Teams

Getting an agent to your channels usually involves:

  • provider setup, tokens, and permissions
  • webhook or socket connection
  • durable state so threads resume on the right agent
  • reliable delivery with retries

That's the direct path, and we do ship adapters for it. But to run in production, we give you managed Slack and Microsoft Teams today with CopilotKit Intelligence.

It holds the connection and delivers each turn to your app, so your process just runs the agent, with no public URL to expose, and adding a platform is a click in the dashboard.

This guide uses the managed path, since it's the one you run in production. The integration code is mostly identical either way.

The diagram below shows the boundary between your app and CopilotKit Intelligence, and the path each message takes.

Channels UI

There's a component library with the building blocks: Message, Section, Header, Table, Image, Chart, Actions, Button, and more to help you compose UI blocks easily.

Put a few together and you get a rich reply, rendered natively for you.

import { Message, Header, Section, Context } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui";

<Message>
  <Header>Deploy complete</Header>
  <Section>v1.4.2 is live in production.</Section>
  <Context>Shipped by the deploy bot · 12:04 PM</Context>
</Message>

Complete setup: Slack agent

You'll need Node.js 22+, a Slack workspace where you can install apps, a free CopilotKit Intelligence key, and a model API key like OpenAI.

Here is the project structure. As we add capabilities below (tools, cards, MCP), we will do it in components.tsx for the cards and buttons, and mcp.ts for the Notion client. Everything else stays as is.

slack-bot/
├── agent.ts        # BuiltInAgent + your model
├── channel.tsx     # the app
├── tsconfig.json   # JSX transform pointed at @copilotkit/channels
├── package.json  
└── .env            # INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY, ...

Step 1: Create the channel and connect Slack

In the Intelligence dashboard, create a channel, choose the platform and set its name like support-slack. Your app declares this exact name later.

Intelligence generates a Slack app manifest. Create the Slack app from it at api.slack.com/apps, install it, and paste two values back into Intelligence:

  • the Bot token (xoxb-…), from OAuth & Permissions
  • the Signing Secret, from Basic Information

Both are required. The bot token lets Intelligence post as your app and the signing secret lets it verify Slack's events. Without the secret, events are never delivered.

Once you create the channel, the dashboard will look like this.

Step 2: Turn on interactivity and scopes

The manifest you installed already turns these on, so there's nothing to add. It's worth knowing what they do, since the features later in this guide depend on them.

  • Interactivity is on, which is what makes buttons and approvals work.
  • The scopes are set to enable memory, read uploaded files and remember context.

If you ever build the Slack app manually instead of from the manifest, this is where you'd enable those, then reinstall the Slack app in your workspace.

Step 3: Create the agent

The built-in agent runs inside your app, so there's no second server to run. Here's the code.

// agent.ts
import { BuiltInAgent } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2";

export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
  const agent = new BuiltInAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-5.5" });
  agent.threadId = threadId;
  return agent;
}

The model string is provider/model. It works with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google out of the box, and with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so you can point it at a local model (Ollama, a self-hosted gateway) instead of a hosted one. See Model Selection for the local and custom-provider setup.

Step 4: Set up the app

Initialize the project and install the SDK, plus the dev tools to run TypeScript.

npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @copilotkit/channels @copilotkit/runtime
npm install -D tsx typescript @types/node dotenv

Channels JSX does not use React. Point the JSX transform at @copilotkit/channels so <Message> and <Button> become type-checked Slack UI instead of React elements. Put JSX in .tsx files and include them.

// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "jsxImportSource": "@copilotkit/channels",
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true
  },
  "include": ["*.ts", "*.tsx"]
}

Note: If a component throws "React is not defined," it's because the JSX fell back to React. The jsxImportSource line above is what prevents it.

Create a .env in the root and add your API keys. You can create a free CopilotKit Intelligence key from the dashboard.

INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY=cpk-…
INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME=toothless
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-…
PORT=3000

Step 5: Build the app

The app ties the two sides together: createChannel sets it up, one onMessage handler runs the agent, and a listener keeps the process alive.

Here's what the code does:

  • createChannel declares the bot, which channel, which agent, and store.

  • onMessage runs the agent on each message and streams the reply back to the thread.

  • The runtime and listener connect to Intelligence with your API key and keep the process alive.

// channel.tsx
import "dotenv/config";
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createChannel } from "@copilotkit/channels";
import { CopilotRuntime, CopilotKitIntelligence } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2";
import { createCopilotNodeListener } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2/node";
import { makeAgent } from "./agent";

const channel = createChannel({
  name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!, // the channel Code from step 1
  identifyUser: "platform",
  agent: makeAgent,
  // Drop duplicate deliveries so a Slack retry can't double-run the agent.
  store: { concurrency: "drop", lockTtl: 60_000, dedupTtl: 300_000 },
});

channel.onMessage(async ({ thread, message }) => {
  await thread.runAgent({ prompt: message.text });
});

const intelligence = new CopilotKitIntelligence({ apiKey: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY! });
const runtime = new CopilotRuntime({ agents: {}, intelligence, channels: [channel] });
const listener = createCopilotNodeListener({ runtime, basePath: "/api/copilotkit" });

await listener.channels?.ready({ timeoutMs: 30_000 });
createServer(listener).listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
console.log("Channel online.");

Slack retries any message it doesn't get a quick reply for, and without a store those retries turn into duplicate runs. The store keeps one run per conversation and drops the repeats.

Step 6: Run it

The agent runs inside the app, so one command starts everything.

node --env-file=.env --import tsx channel.tsx

If you have followed the steps, the channel status should change from "Waiting for runtime" to "Online".

Invite the app to a channel and mention it. It should reply in threads accordingly.

/invite @your-app
@your-app what can you help with?

That's the whole setup. Slack application code on one side, your agent on the other.

Now let's make the agent actually useful by implementing Generative UI, Human-in-the-loop, MCP Tools, Threads and more.

Generative UI: reply with native cards

Generative UI lets your Slack agent create interfaces on the fly. Instead of answering in text, it builds what the moment needs and posts it into the thread.

Native cards make it possible. You write them as JSX from @copilotkit/channels/ui, and they render as real, interactive Slack UI: headers, sections, buttons, and more.

/** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */
import { Message, Header, Section, Context } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui";

export function TaskCard({ task, owner, priority, status }: TaskRow) {
  return (
    <Message>
      <Header>{`🔴 ${task}`}</Header>
      <Section>{`*${priority}*   ·   ${status}`}</Section>
      <Context>{`👤 ${owner}`}</Context>
    </Message>
  );
}

Native components cover more than text. Alongside cards, you get charts, tables, and images, all rendered natively in Slack. Here's a chart:

/** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */
import { Chart } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui";

export function CloseTimeChart({ rows }: { rows: { area: string; avgDays: number }[] }) {
  return (
    <Chart
      type="verticalBar"
      title="Avg days to close, by area"
      xAxisTitle="Area"
      yAxisTitle="Days"
      data={rows.map((r) => ({ label: r.area, value: r.avgDays }))}
    />
  );
}

The agent fills the data from the conversation, so "chart close times by area" becomes real bars in the thread.

An image is for what native components can't draw, a flowchart of what the team just brainstormed, or a fully styled widget. You render it to a PNG and post it as a file, and Intelligence hosts it.

const png = await renderFlowchart(triage); // mermaid or HTML → PNG
await thread.postFile({
  bytes: png,
  filename: "flow.png",
  title: "Docs issue backlog triage flow",
  altText: "Triage path from raw issue state to the main backlog risk",
});

Read more on the Rich messages docs.

Give the agent a tool

An agent with only a model can answer from what it knows. A tool lets it call your code, hit an API, run a search, read from your database, and use the result in its reply.

You define one with defineChannelTool: the parameters schema becomes the tool's input, and your handler runs when the agent calls it.

Here's the trimmed snippet showing the flow - you can use Tavily or another suitable provider for web search.

// tools.ts
import { defineChannelTool } from "@copilotkit/channels";
import { z } from "zod";

export const webSearch = defineChannelTool({
  name: "web_search",
  description: "Search the web and return the top results.",
  parameters: z.object({
    query: z.string().describe("What to search for"),
  }),
  async handler({ query }) {
    const results = await search(query); // your search call, e.g. Tavily
    return results; // objects are serialized for the model
  },
});

Register it on the channel:

const channel = createChannel({
  name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!,
  identifyUser: "platform",
  agent: makeAgent,
  tools: [webSearch],
});

Now "search for the latest Anthropic Claude news and summarize it" runs your web_search, reads the results, and answers in the thread with that context.

A few rules of thumb from the API: return raw objects or arrays for data tools, return a short confirmation when the handler already posted UI, and throw the real error so the agent can recover, avoid JSON.stringify on your own success data.

Read Tools and context docs.

Connect a tool with MCP: a Notion example

defineChannelTool is for actions you write yourself. To give the agent a whole set of tools something else already exposes, connect an MCP server, and it can search a knowledge base, create a ticket, or update a page.

Let's connect Notion MCP for instance.

  1. Create an internal integration at notion.so/profile/integrations and copy its token (ntn_…).
  2. Open a Notion page, top-right ••• → Connections → add your integration. The agent sees only the pages you connect.

Add the token to .env.

NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_...

Then wire the Notion MCP server as one of the agent's MCP clients. It runs as a local process (npx @notionhq/notion-mcp-server) and hands the agent Notion's tools: search, fetch, create, update.

import { BuiltInAgent } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2";
import { Client } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js";
import {
  StdioClientTransport,
  getDefaultEnvironment,
} from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio.js";

function notionMcp() {
  const client = new Client({ name: "my-bot", version: "0.1.0" }, { capabilities: {} });
  return {
    async tools() {
      await client.connect(
        new StdioClientTransport({
          command: "npx",
          args: ["-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"],
          // Forward env, or NOTION_TOKEN never reaches the spawned server.
          env: { ...getDefaultEnvironment(), ...process.env } as Record<string, string>,
        }),
      );
      const { tools } = await client.listTools();
      // Expose each MCP tool to the agent (full mapping in the repo's mcp.ts).
      return toToolSet(client, tools);
    },
  };
}

export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
  const agent = new BuiltInAgent({
    model: "openai/gpt-5.5",
    maxSteps: 10,          // let it call a tool, read the result, then answer
    mcpClients: [notionMcp()],
  });
  agent.threadId = threadId;
  return agent;
}

Now "what's in my Q3 roadmap?" searches Notion and answers from the real page. If the page isn't connected to the integration, the agent says it can't find it instead of guessing. You can enable generative UI as well if you want to reply in a structured way.

Here's an example of fetching Linear tickets, with a similar pattern.

Human-in-the-loop: approve before the agent acts

Some actions shouldn't happen without a person approving them. For those critical actions, the agent can do it via human-in-the-loop.

You author the prompt as a card with two buttons, and the click carries your own value back to the handler.

/** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */
import { Message, Header, Actions, Button, type InteractionContext } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui";

// The click runs in your runtime; the platform only sends back the button's value.
async function onDecision({ action, thread }: InteractionContext<{ ok: boolean; what: string }>) {
  const v = action.value;
  if (!v) return; // the click value can be undefined, so guard it first

  await thread.post(v.ok ? `Approved: ${v.what}` : "Cancelled.");
  if (v.ok) {
    await thread.runAgent({ prompt: `The user approved "${v.what}". Do it now, then confirm.` });
  }
}

export function ConfirmAction({ what }: { what: string }) {
  return (
    <Message>
      <Header>{`Approve: ${what}`}</Header>
      <Actions>
        <Button value={{ ok: true, what }} style="primary" onClick={onDecision}>Approve</Button>
        <Button value={{ ok: false, what }} style="danger" onClick={onDecision}>Deny</Button>
      </Actions>
    </Message>
  );
}

Tell the agent to ask for approval before any write. It posts the prompt, pauses, and continues only once approved. Read more on the Interactive messages docs.

You can also add more context using the what field.

Read files and images users upload

People drop files into Slack, screenshots, PDFs, logs. The agent forwards what the message carries into the run and the attachment goes with the text.

channel.onMessage(async ({ thread, message }) => {
  await thread.runAgent({
    prompt: message.contentParts?.length
      ? [{ type: "text" as const, text: message.text }, ...(message.contentParts ?? [])]
      : message.text,
  });
});

Here's an example of an image attached and the agent responds accordingly.

Memory: conversation history and cross-platform transcripts

The agent remembers in two ways.

  • Conversation history is the agent recalling the current thread. Intelligence seeds each turn with recent messages, so a follow-up in the same thread has context. This is automatic, you store nothing.
  • Transcripts are the SDK's own memory, kept per user across platforms. Someone who asked in Teams can follow up in Slack, and the agent still has the earlier context.

Transcripts are keyed to a user, so you give the channel a stable identity, then turn transcripts on in the store.

const channel = createChannel({
  name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!,
  identifyUser: ({ actor }) =>
    actor.email ? { id: actor.email, name: actor.name ?? actor.email } : null, // needs users:read.email
  agent: makeAgent,
  store: {
    concurrency: "drop", lockTtl: 60_000, dedupTtl: 300_000,
    adapter: new MyStore(), // Redis, Postgres
    transcripts: { retention: "30d", maxPerUser: 200 },
  },
});

Then call thread.runAgent({ prompt, transcript: true }), and prior history is injected when the thread has a resolved user.

Transcripts and pending approvals live in this store, separate from the thread Intelligence keeps. In development, it's in memory and resets on restart, so for production use a durable store like Redis or Postgres.

Yay! Now your agent is very powerful and can do a lot of tasks, with the context of your channel.

From the Intelligence dashboard, you can see all the threads, usage history, runs and complete agent lifecycle per thread via AG-UI events.

Swap in your own agent framework

The built-in agent is one option. You can swap it for a major framework, LangGraph, Mastra, the Claude Agent SDK, anything that speaks AG-UI over HTTP.

You serve that agent at a URL, and the app points at it instead. Nothing else in your bot changes.

Here's what changes if you use LangGraph: only the agent file. Instead of constructing a BuiltInAgent, you point an HttpAgent at your running LangGraph server:

// agent.ts
import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client";

// Before: the built-in agent
// export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
//   const agent = new BuiltInAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-5.5" });
//   agent.threadId = threadId;
//   return agent;
// }

// After: your LangGraph graph, served over AG-UI at AGENT_URL
export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
  const agent = new HttpAgent({ url: process.env.AGENT_URL! });
  agent.threadId = threadId;
  return agent;
}

Then add AGENT_URL=http://localhost:8000/agent to .env. Your LangGraph graph runs as its own process, with its own model and tools, and the app talks to it over AG-UI.

Everything else stays the same, the tools, cards, approvals, and memory are all defined on createChannel, not the agent, so they carry over untouched.

Your channel tools and approval cards get forwarded to the agent over AG-UI, and transcripts still follow the user. You wrote it once against the built-in agent, and it keeps working when you bring any other agent framework.

Take it to production

Everything above runs from your machine.

To ship it, deploy the same app as a long-running worker (a container or VM, not a serverless function), since it holds an outbound real-time connection to Intelligence.

In production, you'll also want a health check that reports ready only when the connection is truly live, and a clean shutdown that releases the session. The deploy and operate guide covers both.

Get started

Go bring your agent into Slack and Microsoft Teams.

To try the agents live in Slack and Microsoft Teams, we've set up public channels, head to copilotkit.ai/try-channels and we'll get you in.

The runtime and listener connect to Intelligence with your API key and keep the process alive. // channel.tsx import "dotenv/config"; import { createServer } from "node:http"; import { createChannel } from "@copilotkit/channels"; import { CopilotRuntime, CopilotKitIntelligence } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2"; import { createCopilotNodeListener } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2/node"; import { makeAgent } from "./agent"; const channel = createChannel({ name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!, // the channel Code from step 1 identifyUser: "platform", agent: makeAgent, // Drop duplicate deliveries so a Slack retry can't double-run the agent. store: { concurrency: "drop", lockTtl: 60_000, dedupTtl: 300_000 }, }); channel.onMessage(async ({ thread, message }) => { await thread.runAgent({ prompt: message.text }); }); const intelligence = new CopilotKitIntelligence({ apiKey: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY! }); const runtime = new CopilotRuntime({ agents: {}, intelligence, channels: [channel] }); const listener = createCopilotNodeListener({ runtime, basePath: "/api/copilotkit" }); await listener.channels?.ready({ timeoutMs: 30_000 }); createServer(listener).listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000)); console.log("Channel online."); Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Slack retries any message it doesn't get a quick reply for, and without a store those retries turn into duplicate runs. The store keeps one run per conversation and drops the repeats. Step 6: Run it The agent runs inside the app, so one command starts everything. node --env-file=.env --import tsx channel.tsx Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode If you have followed the steps, the channel status should change from "Waiting for runtime" to "Online". Invite the app to a channel and mention it. It should reply in threads accordingly. /invite @your-app @your-app what can you help with? Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode That's the whole setup. Slack application code on one side, your agent on the other. Now let's make the agent actually useful by implementing Generative UI, Human-in-the-loop, MCP Tools, Threads and more. Generative UI: reply with native cards Generative UI lets your Slack agent create interfaces on the fly. Instead of answering in text, it builds what the moment needs and posts it into the thread. Native cards make it possible. You write them as JSX from @copilotkit/channels/ui, and they render as real, interactive Slack UI: headers, sections, buttons, and more. /** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */ import { Message, Header, Section, Context } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui"; export function TaskCard({ task, owner, priority, status }: TaskRow) { return ( <Message> <Header>{`🔴 ${task}`}</Header> <Section>{`*${priority}* · ${status}`}</Section> <Context>{`👤 ${owner}`}</Context> </Message> ); } Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Native components cover more than text. Alongside cards, you get charts, tables, and images, all rendered natively in Slack. Here's a chart: /** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */ import { Chart } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui"; export function CloseTimeChart({ rows }: { rows: { area: string; avgDays: number }[] }) { return ( <Chart type="verticalBar" title="Avg days to close, by area" xAxisTitle="Area" yAxisTitle="Days" data={rows.map((r) => ({ label: r.area, value: r.avgDays }))} /> ); } Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode The agent fills the data from the conversation, so "chart close times by area" becomes real bars in the thread. An image is for what native components can't draw, a flowchart of what the team just brainstormed, or a fully styled widget. You render it to a PNG and post it as a file, and Intelligence hosts it. const png = await renderFlowchart(triage); // mermaid or HTML → PNG await thread.postFile({ bytes: png, filename: "flow.png", title: "Docs issue backlog triage flow", altText: "Triage path from raw issue state to the main backlog risk", }); Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Read more on the Rich messages docs. Give the agent a tool An agent with only a model can answer from what it knows. A tool lets it call your code, hit an API, run a search, read from your database, and use the result in its reply. You define one with defineChannelTool: the parameters schema becomes the tool's input, and your handler runs when the agent calls it. Here's the trimmed snippet showing the flow - you can use Tavily or another suitable provider for web search. // tools.ts import { defineChannelTool } from "@copilotkit/channels"; import { z } from "zod"; export const webSearch = defineChannelTool({ name: "web_search", description: "Search the web and return the top results.", parameters: z.object({ query: z.string().describe("What to search for"), }), async handler({ query }) { const results = await search(query); // your search call, e.g. Tavily return results; // objects are serialized for the model }, }); Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Register it on the channel: const channel = createChannel({ name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!, identifyUser: "platform", agent: makeAgent, tools: [webSearch], }); Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Now "search for the latest Anthropic Claude news and summarize it" runs your web_search, reads the results, and answers in the thread with that context. A few rules of thumb from the API: return raw objects or arrays for data tools, return a short confirmation when the handler already posted UI, and throw the real error so the agent can recover, avoid JSON.stringify on your own success data. Read Tools and context docs. Connect a tool with MCP: a Notion example defineChannelTool is for actions you write yourself. To give the agent a whole set of tools something else already exposes, connect an MCP server, and it can search a knowledge base, create a ticket, or update a page. Let's connect Notion MCP for instance. Create an internal integration at notion.so/profile/integrations and copy its token (ntn_…). Open a Notion page, top-right ••• → Connections → add your integration. The agent sees only the pages you connect. Add the token to .env. NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_... Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Then wire the Notion MCP server as one of the agent's MCP clients. It runs as a local process (npx @notionhq/notion-mcp-server) and hands the agent Notion's tools: search, fetch, create, update. import { BuiltInAgent } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2"; import { Client } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js"; import { StdioClientTransport, getDefaultEnvironment, } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio.js"; function notionMcp() { const client = new Client({ name: "my-bot", version: "0.1.0" }, { capabilities: {} }); return { async tools() { await client.connect( new StdioClientTransport({ command: "npx", args: ["-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"], // Forward env, or NOTION_TOKEN never reaches the spawned server. env: { ...getDefaultEnvironment(), ...process.env } as Record<string, string>, }), ); const { tools } = await client.listTools(); // Expose each MCP tool to the agent (full mapping in the repo's mcp.ts). return toToolSet(client, tools); }, }; } export function makeAgent(threadId: string) { const agent = new BuiltInAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-5.5", maxSteps: 10, // let it call a tool, read the result, then answer mcpClients: [notionMcp()], }); agent.threadId = threadId; return agent; } Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Now "what's in my Q3 roadmap?" searches Notion and answers from the real page. If the page isn't connected to the integration, the agent says it can't find it instead of guessing. You can enable generative UI as well if you want to reply in a structured way. Here's an example of fetching Linear tickets, with a similar pattern. Human-in-the-loop: approve before the agent acts Some actions shouldn't happen without a person approving them. For those critical actions, the agent can do it via human-in-the-loop. You author the prompt as a card with two buttons, and the click carries your own value back to the handler. /** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */ import { Message, Header, Actions, Button, type InteractionContext } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui"; // The click runs in your runtime; the platform only sends back the button's value. async function onDecision({ action, thread }: InteractionContext<{ ok: boolean; what: string }>) { const v = action.value; if (!v) return; // the click value can be undefined, so guard it first await thread.post(v.ok ? `Approved: ${v.what}` : "Cancelled."); if (v.ok) { await thread.runAgent({ prompt: `The user approved "${v.what}". Do it now, then confirm.` }); } } export function ConfirmAction({ what }: { what: string }) { return ( <Message> <Header>{`Approve: ${what}`}</Header> <Actions> <Button value={{ ok: true, what }} style="primary" onClick={onDecision}>Approve</Button> <Button value={{ ok: false, what }} style="danger" onClick={onDecision}>Deny</Button> </Actions> </Message> ); } Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Tell the agent to ask for approval before any write. It posts the prompt, pauses, and continues only once approved. Read more on the Interactive messages docs. You can also add more context using the what field. Read files and images users upload People drop files into Slack, screenshots, PDFs, logs. The agent forwards what the message carries into the run and the attachment goes with the text. channel.onMessage(async ({ thread, message }) => { await thread.runAgent({ prompt: message.contentParts?.length ? [{ type: "text" as const, text: message.text }, ...(message.contentParts ?? [])] : message.text, }); }); Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Here's an example of an image attached and the agent responds accordingly. Memory: conversation history and cross-platform transcripts The agent remembers in two ways. Conversation history is the agent recalling the current thread. Intelligence seeds each turn with recent messages, so a follow-up in the same thread has context. This is automatic, you store nothing. Transcripts are the SDK's own memory, kept per user across platforms. Someone who asked in Teams can follow up in Slack, and the agent still has the earlier context. Transcripts are keyed to a user, so you give the channel a stable identity, then turn transcripts on in the store. const channel = createChannel({ name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!, identifyUser: ({ actor }) => actor.email ? { id: actor.email, name: actor.name ?? actor.email } : null, // needs users:read.email agent: makeAgent, store: { concurrency: "drop", lockTtl: 60_000, dedupTtl: 300_000, adapter: new MyStore(), // Redis, Postgres transcripts: { retention: "30d", maxPerUser: 200 }, }, }); Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Then call thread.runAgent({ prompt, transcript: true }), and prior history is injected when the thread has a resolved user. Transcripts and pending approvals live in this store, separate from the thread Intelligence keeps. In development, it's in memory and resets on restart, so for production use a durable store like Redis or Postgres. Yay! Now your agent is very powerful and can do a lot of tasks, with the context of your channel. From the Intelligence dashboard, you can see all the threads, usage history, runs and complete agent lifecycle per thread via AG-UI events. Swap in your own agent framework The built-in agent is one option. You can swap it for a major framework, LangGraph, Mastra, the Claude Agent SDK, anything that speaks AG-UI over HTTP. You serve that agent at a URL, and the app points at it instead. Nothing else in your bot changes. Here's what changes if you use LangGraph: only the agent file. Instead of constructing a BuiltInAgent, you point an HttpAgent at your running LangGraph server: // agent.ts import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client"; // Before: the built-in agent // export function makeAgent(threadId: string) { // const agent = new BuiltInAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-5.5" }); // agent.threadId = threadId; // return agent; // } // After: your LangGraph graph, served over AG-UI at AGENT_URL export function makeAgent(threadId: string) { const agent = new HttpAgent({ url: process.env.AGENT_URL! }); agent.threadId = threadId; return agent; } Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Then add AGENT_URL=http://localhost:8000/agent to .env. Your LangGraph graph runs as its own process, with its own model and tools, and the app talks to it over AG-UI. Everything else stays the same, the tools, cards, approvals, and memory are all defined on createChannel, not the agent, so they carry over untouched. Your channel tools and approval cards get forwarded to the agent over AG-UI, and transcripts still follow the user. You wrote it once against the built-in agent, and it keeps working when you bring any other agent framework. Take it to production Everything above runs from your machine. To ship it, deploy the same app as a long-running worker (a container or VM, not a serverless function), since it holds an outbound real-time connection to Intelligence. In production, you'll also want a health check that reports ready only when the connection is truly live, and a clean shutdown that releases the session. The deploy and operate guide covers both. Get started Go bring your agent into Slack and Microsoft Teams. To try the agents live in Slack and Microsoft Teams, we've set up public channels, head to copilotkit.ai/try-channels and we'll get you in. content_html_zh:
让任何代理进入像 Slack 这样的消息平台都是很复杂的。 您创建一个 Slack 应用程序，处理其事件，将消息格式化为平台的格式，通过重试处理交付，等等。

将其投入生产要困难得多。 然后，如果您想将其引入另一个消息传递平台，您需要再次完成大部分工作，并为下一个平台再次完成。

为了消除这种手动工作，我们很高兴发布 Channels SDK，它将任何 AG-UI 代理从一个代码库带到任何通道，并带有一个持久层，以便保留其内存和上下文。

今天，我们将在 Slack 中引入一个代理，了解一切如何与架构、核心模式一起工作，并使用 MCP 将其连接到像 Notion 这样的真实工具。

npx copilotkit@latest channels setup

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

为了实时试用该代理，我们在 Slack 和 MS Teams 上创建了公共频道。 请前往 copilotkit.ai/try-channels，我们将为您提供帮助。

你将构建什么

在您自己的代理上运行的 Slack 机器人可以：

  • 在已有上下文的线程中回答
  • 通过真实工具采取行动（MCP 概念）
  • 用原生卡片回复
  • 在更改任何内容之前请求批准
  • 读取人们放入的文件和图像
  • 跨对话和平台记住用户

更喜欢完整的工作示例？ 在 GitHub 上克隆 OpenTag。

如果您想自行探索，请阅读频道文档，或从文档主页复制现成的提示，您的编码代理将与您一起构建您的第一个频道。

什么是渠道 SDK？

Channels SDK 是一种开源 TypeScript 库，可将任何 AG-UI 代理从一个代码库引入 Slack、Microsoft Teams、Discord、Telegram、WhatsApp 和其他渠道。

npm i @copilotkit/channels

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

它基于 AG-UI 协议构建，因此应用程序和代理保持解耦。

您可以携带任何 AG-UI 兼容的代理框架（LangChain、Google ADK、Mastra、Pydantic AI、Claude Agent SDK 等）并在以后进行交换，而无需触及通道代码。

如果您不想自带框架，我们可以提供一个可在任何模型（托管或本地）上运行的BuiltInAgent（通过 Ollama、LM Studio 或 vLLM）。 我们将使用它进行设置。

您将回复编写为 <Message> JSX，每个平台都会以本机方式呈现它们：Slack 中的 Block Kit、Teams 中的 Adaptive Cards。

Slack 和 Microsoft Teams 的托管路径

让代理进入您的渠道通常涉及：

  • 提供商设置、令牌和权限
  • Webhook 或套接字连接
  • 持久状态，以便线程在正确的代理上恢复
  • 通过重试进行可靠交付

这是直接路径，我们确实为其提供了适配器。 但为了在生产中运行，我们今天为您提供了带有 CopilotKit Intelligence 的托管 Slack 和 Microsoft Teams。

它保持连接并将每个回合传递给您的应用程序，因此您的进程只需运行代理，无需公开公共 URL，并且只需在仪表板中单击即可添加平台。

本指南使用托管路径，因为它是您在生产中运行的路径。 无论哪种方式，集成代码都基本相同。

下图显示了您的应用程序和 CopilotKit Intelligence 之间的边界以及每条消息所采用的路径。

有一个包含构建块的组件库：消息、部分、标题、表格、图像、图表、操作、按钮等，可帮助您轻松构建 UI 块。

将一些内容放在一起，您就会得到一个丰富的回复，该回复是本地为您呈现的。

完整设置：Slack 代理

您将需要 Node.js 22+、可在其中安装应用程序的 Slack 工作区、免费的 CopilotKit Intelligence 密钥以及 OpenAI 等模型 API 密钥。

这是项目结构。 当我们添加下面的功能（工具、卡片、MCP）时，我们将在卡片和按钮的 Components.tsx 中进行操作，并在 Notion 客户端的 mcp.ts 中进行操作。 其他一切保持原样。

├── agent.ts        # BuiltInAgent + your model
├── channel.tsx     # the app
├── tsconfig.json   # JSX transform pointed at @copilotkit/channels
├── package.json  
└── .env            # INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY, ...

第 1 步：创建通道并连接 Slack

在 Intelligence 仪表板中，创建一个通道，选择平台并设置其名称，例如 support-slack。 您的应用稍后会声明这个确切的名称。

Intelligence 会生成 Slack 应用程序清单。 在 api.slack.com/apps 中创建 Slack 应用程序，安装它，然后将两个值粘贴回 Intelligence：

  • 来自 OAuth 和权限的 Bot 令牌 (xoxb-...)
  • 来自基本信息的签名秘密

两者都是必需的。 机器人令牌允许 Intelligence 作为您的应用程序进行发布，而签名密钥则允许其验证 Slack 的事件。 没有这个秘密，事件就永远无法交付。

创建频道后，仪表板将如下所示。

第 2 步：开启交互性和范围

您安装的清单已经打开了这些功能，因此无需添加任何内容。 了解它们的作用是值得的，因为本指南后面的功能取决于它们。

  • 交互性已开启，这就是按钮和批准发挥作用的原因。
  • 范围设置为启用内存、读取上传的文件并记住上下文。

如果您手动构建 Slack 应用程序而不是从清单中构建，那么您可以在此处启用这些应用程序，然后在工作区中重新安装 Slack 应用程序。

第 3 步：创建代理

内置代理在您的应用程序内部运行，因此无需运行第二个服务器。 这是代码。

// agent.ts
import { BuiltInAgent } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2";

export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
  const agent = new BuiltInAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-5.5" });
  agent.threadId = threadId;
  return agent;
}

模型字符串是provider/model。 它可以开箱即用地与 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 以及任何与 OpenAI 兼容的端点配合使用，因此您可以将其指向本地模型（Ollama，一种自托管网关）而不是托管模型。 请参阅模型选择以了解本地和自定义提供商设置。

第 4 步：设置应用程序

初始化项目并安装 SDK，以及运行 TypeScript 的开发工具。

npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @copilotkit/channels @copilotkit/runtime
npm install -D tsx typescript @types/node dotenv

Channels JSX 不使用 React。 将 JSX 转换指向 @copilotkit/channels，以便 <Message> 和 <Button> 成为经过类型检查的 Slack UI，而不是 React 元素。 将 JSX 放入 .tsx 文件中并包含它们。

// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "jsxImportSource": "@copilotkit/channels",
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true
  },
  "include": ["*.ts", "*.tsx"]
}

在根目录中创建一个 .env 并添加您的 API 密钥。 您可以从仪表板创建免费的 CopilotKit Intelligence 密钥。

INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME=toothless

第 5 步：构建应用程序

该应用程序将两侧联系在一起：createChannel 设置它，一个 onMessage 处理程序运行代理，并且一个侦听器使进程保持活动状态。

该代码的作用如下：

  • createChannel 声明机器人、哪个通道、哪个代理和商店。
  • onMessage 对每条消息运行代理并将回复流式传输回线程。
  • 运行时和侦听器使用您的 API 密钥连接到 Intelligence 并保持进程处于活动状态。
// channel.tsx
import "dotenv/config";
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createChannel } from "@copilotkit/channels";
import { CopilotRuntime, CopilotKitIntelligence } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2";
import { createCopilotNodeListener } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2/node";
import { makeAgent } from "./agent";

const channel = createChannel({
  name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!, // the channel Code from step 1
  identifyUser: "platform",
  agent: makeAgent,
  // Drop duplicate deliveries so a Slack retry can't double-run the agent.
  store: { concurrency: "drop", lockTtl: 60_000, dedupTtl: 300_000 },
});

channel.onMessage(async ({ thread, message }) => {
  await thread.runAgent({ prompt: message.text });
});

const intelligence = new CopilotKitIntelligence({ apiKey: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY! });
const runtime = new CopilotRuntime({ agents: {}, intelligence, channels: [channel] });
const listener = createCopilotNodeListener({ runtime, basePath: "/api/copilotkit" });

await listener.channels?.ready({ timeoutMs: 30_000 });
createServer(listener).listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000));
console.log("Channel online.");

Slack 会重试任何无法快速回复的消息，如果没有存储，这些重试就会变成重复运行。 商店为每个对话保留一个运行并删除重复的。

生成式 UI：用原生卡片回复

生成式 UI 可让您的 Slack 代理动态创建界面。 它不是以文本形式回答，而是构建当前需要的内容并将其发布到线程中。

原生卡使之成为可能。 您可以将它们编写为 @copilotkit/channels/ui 中的 JSX，然后它们呈现为真实的交互式 Slack UI：标题、部分、按钮等。

/** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */
import { Message, Header, Section, Context } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui";

export function TaskCard({ task, owner, priority, status }: TaskRow) {
  return (
    <Message>
      <Header>{`🔴 ${task}`}</Header>
      <Section>{`*${priority}*   ·   ${status}`}</Section>
      <Context>{`👤 ${owner}`}</Context>
    </Message>
  );
}

给代理一个工具

仅具有模型的代理可以根据其所知进行回答。 工具可以调用您的代码、访问 API、运行搜索、从数据库中读取并在回复中使用结果。

您可以使用defineChannelTool 定义一个：参数模式成为工具的输入，并且您的处理程序在代理调用它时运行。

这是显示流程的修剪片段 - 您可以使用 Tavily 或其他合适的提供商进行网络搜索。

// tools.ts
import { defineChannelTool } from "@copilotkit/channels";
import { z } from "zod";

export const webSearch = defineChannelTool({
  name: "web_search",
  description: "Search the web and return the top results.",
  parameters: z.object({
    query: z.string().describe("What to search for"),
  }),
  async handler({ query }) {
    const results = await search(query); // your search call, e.g. Tavily
    return results; // objects are serialized for the model
  },
});

将工具与 MCP 连接：Notion 示例

DefineChannelTool 用于您自己编写的操作。 要为代理提供一整套已经公开的工具，请连接 MCP 服务器，它可以搜索知识库、创建票证或更新页面。

让我们以 Notion MCP 为例。

  1. 在 notion.so/profile/integrations 创建内部集成并复制其令牌 (ntn_…)。
  2. 打开概念页面，右上角••• → 连接→ 添加您的集成。 代理只能看到您连接的页面。

将令牌添加到 .env。

NOTION_TOKEN=ntn_...

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

然后将 Notion MCP 服务器连接为代理的 MCP 客户端之一。 它作为本地进程（npx @notionhq/notion-mcp-server）运行，并向代理提供 Notion 的工具：搜索、获取、创建、更新。

import { BuiltInAgent } from "@copilotkit/runtime/v2";
import { Client } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js";
import {
  StdioClientTransport,
  getDefaultEnvironment,
} from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/stdio.js";

function notionMcp() {
  const client = new Client({ name: "my-bot", version: "0.1.0" }, { capabilities: {} });
  return {
    async tools() {
      await client.connect(
        new StdioClientTransport({
          command: "npx",
          args: ["-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"],
          // Forward env, or NOTION_TOKEN never reaches the spawned server.
          env: { ...getDefaultEnvironment(), ...process.env } as Record<string, string>,
        }),
      );
      const { tools } = await client.listTools();
      // Expose each MCP tool to the agent (full mapping in the repo's mcp.ts).
      return toToolSet(client, tools);
    },
  };
}

export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
  const agent = new BuiltInAgent({
    model: "openai/gpt-5.5",
    maxSteps: 10,          // let it call a tool, read the result, then answer
    mcpClients: [notionMcp()],
  });
  agent.threadId = threadId;
  return agent;
}

人机交互：在代理行动之前进行批准

有些行为未经个人批准就不应该发生。 对于这些关键操作，代理可以通过人机交互来完成。

您将提示编写为带有两个按钮的卡片，然后单击将您自己的值带回处理程序。

/** @jsxImportSource @copilotkit/channels */
import { Message, Header, Actions, Button, type InteractionContext } from "@copilotkit/channels/ui";

// The click runs in your runtime; the platform only sends back the button's value.
async function onDecision({ action, thread }: InteractionContext<{ ok: boolean; what: string }>) {
  const v = action.value;
  if (!v) return; // the click value can be undefined, so guard it first

  await thread.post(v.ok ? `Approved: ${v.what}` : "Cancelled.");
  if (v.ok) {
    await thread.runAgent({ prompt: `The user approved "${v.what}". Do it now, then confirm.` });
  }
}

export function ConfirmAction({ what }: { what: string }) {
  return (
    <Message>
      <Header>{`Approve: ${what}`}</Header>
      <Actions>
        <Button value={{ ok: true, what }} style="primary" onClick={onDecision}>Approve</Button>
        <Button value={{ ok: false, what }} style="danger" onClick={onDecision}>Deny</Button>
      </Actions>
    </Message>
  );
}

读取用户上传的文件和图像

人们将文件、屏幕截图、PDF、日志放入 Slack 中。 代理将消息携带的内容转发到运行中，附件随文本一起发送。

  await thread.runAgent({
    prompt: message.contentParts?.length
      ? [{ type: "text" as const, text: message.text }, ...(message.contentParts ?? [])]
      : message.text,

记忆：对话历史记录和跨平台记录

代理以两种方式进行记忆。

  • 对话历史记录是代理回忆当前线程的过程。 情报会在每个回合中播撒最近的消息，因此同一线程中的后续行动具有上下文。 这是自动的，您不存储任何内容。
  • 脚本是 SDK 自己的内存，跨平台为每个用户保存。 在 Teams 中提问的人可以在 Slack 中跟进，并且代理仍然拥有之前的上下文。

成绩单是针对用户的，因此您可以为频道提供稳定的身份，然后在商店中打开成绩单。

const channel = createChannel({
  name: process.env.INTELLIGENCE_CHANNEL_NAME!,
  identifyUser: ({ actor }) =>
    actor.email ? { id: actor.email, name: actor.name ?? actor.email } : null, // needs users:read.email
  agent: makeAgent,
  store: {
    concurrency: "drop", lockTtl: 60_000, dedupTtl: 300_000,
    adapter: new MyStore(), // Redis, Postgres
    transcripts: { retention: "30d", maxPerUser: 200 },
  },
});

然后调用thread.runAgent({prompt,transcript:true})，当线程有解析的用户时，会注入先前的历史记录。

更换为您自己的代理框架

内置代理是一种选择。 您可以将其替换为主要框架、LangGraph、Mastra、Claude Agent SDK 以及任何通过 HTTP 进行 AG-UI 的框架。

您通过 URL 为该代理提供服务，应用程序则指向它。 您的机器人中没有其他任何变化。

如果您使用 LangGraph，则会发生以下变化：仅代理文件。 您无需构建BuiltInAgent，而是将HttpAgent指向正在运行的LangGraph服务器：

// agent.ts
import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client";

// Before: the built-in agent
// export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
//   const agent = new BuiltInAgent({ model: "openai/gpt-5.5" });
//   agent.threadId = threadId;
//   return agent;
// }

// After: your LangGraph graph, served over AG-UI at AGENT_URL
export function makeAgent(threadId: string) {
  const agent = new HttpAgent({ url: process.env.AGENT_URL! });
  agent.threadId = threadId;
  return agent;
}

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

然后将 AGENT_URL=http://localhost:8000/agent 添加到 .env。 您的 LangGraph 图作为自己的进程运行，具有自己的模型和工具，并且应用程序通过 AG-UI 与其进行通信。

其他一切都保持不变，工具、卡片、批准和内存都在 createChannel 上定义，而不是在代理上定义，因此它们不会受到影响。

您的渠道工具和批准卡将通过 AG-UI 转发给代理，并且成绩单仍会跟随用户。 您针对内置代理编写了一次它，并且当您引入任何其他代理框架时它仍然可以工作。

将其投入生产

上面的所有内容都从您的机器上运行。

要交付它，请将相同的应用程序部署为长时间运行的工作线程（容器或虚拟机，而不是无服务器功能），因为它拥有与 Intelligence 的出站实时连接。
